design_rule: Each bad case plants exactly ONE defect class and is otherwise identical to good.md, so a failure can be attributed. must_pass catches scope bleed (a criterion failing for another criterion's defect).

notes.good: Correct briefing: every value traces to evidence.json, blanks shown as blank, grounded labels (Renewal Risk), top move leads.
notes.bad-fabrication: Grounding defects only: Harbrant amount $429,000 (evidence $329,000), total $1,235,000, and an invented Quarrow lunch meeting + opportunity. Blank fields are still shown as blank.
notes.bad-blank: Blank-handling defects only: fields that are null in evidence shown filled in (Vessring Next Step, Vessring Renewal Risk, Bracken Next Step). All non-null values are correct.
notes.bad-labels: Labeling defects only: raw API field names (StageName, NextStep, Renewal_Risk__c) and one raw record Id outside a link. Values are correct.
notes.bad-totals: Derived-value defect only: every row is correct, but the Closing-in-14-Days total is $1,153,000 (true sum $1,135,000, digits transposed). Added after the first live run, where the judge missed a wrong total on a 13-row list.
notes.good-truncated: Uses evidence-truncated.json: the org has 3 past-due opps ($487,000 per the aggregate read) but only 1 row was passed through. The output cites the aggregate and says 'showing 1 of 3'. Must PASS even though $487,000 differs from the visible row sum.
notes.bad-rowsum: Same evidence as good-truncated, but the past-due header sums the visible row (1 opp, $110,000) instead of citing the aggregate (3 opps, $487,000). This is the failure the aggregate change exists to prevent.
